subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Adding sugar in high concentration, as in making jam, preserves the fruit by:
options: Drawing water out of microbes so they cannot grow
questions.explain: A high sugar concentration draws water out of microbes by osmosis, stopping them growing.

questions.q: 'Folding' is a gentle technique used mainly to:
options: Combine ingredients while keeping air in the mixture
questions.explain: Folding gently combines ingredients, such as flour into a whisked sponge, while keeping trapped air.

questions.q: The safest way to hold food still while cutting it with a knife is using the:
questions.explain: The bridge and claw grips keep fingers safely away from the blade while cutting.

questions.q: Why is accurate weighing and measuring of ingredients important in baking?
options: It ensures the correct chemical reactions, texture and consistent results
questions.explain: Accurate measuring ensures recipes work correctly, giving the right texture, rise and consistent results.

questions.q: What is the main function of eggs in a baked Yorkshire pudding batter?
options: To set the structure through coagulation and help it rise
questions.explain: Eggs coagulate on heating to set the structure and help the batter rise.

questions.q: Grilling is often considered a healthier cooking method than frying because it:
options: Allows fat to drain away from the food
questions.explain: Grilling allows fat to drip away from the food rather than being absorbed, reducing fat content.

questions.q: When using a sharp knife, the blade should always be:
options: Sharp and the cutting motion directed away from the body
questions.explain: A sharp knife is safer than a blunt one, and cutting away from the body reduces the risk of injury.

questions.q: Which cooking method best retains water-soluble vitamins such as vitamin C?
questions.explain: Steaming reduces contact with water, so fewer water-soluble vitamins like vitamin C are lost.

questions.q: Which cooking method involves cooking food in dry heat in an oven, often with fat, such as for meat or potatoes?
questions.explain: Roasting cooks food using dry heat in an oven, usually with some fat or oil.

questions.q: What is the main function of sugar when making a creamed sponge cake?
options: To bind the ingredients like a protein
To make the cake rise as a raising agent
To thicken the mixture like starch
To add sweetness and help trap air when creamed with fat
questions.explain: Sugar sweetens and, when creamed with fat, helps incorporate air to give a light texture.

questions.q: 'Blanching' vegetables before freezing is done mainly to:
options: Destroy enzymes that would spoil colour and flavour
questions.explain: Brief blanching inactivates enzymes that would otherwise cause loss of colour, texture and flavour during freezing.

questions.q: Pickling food in vinegar preserves it mainly because the vinegar:
options: Creates an acidic environment in which bacteria cannot easily grow
questions.explain: Vinegar lowers the pH, creating acidic conditions that inhibit bacterial growth.

questions.q: What is the main function of fat when shortcrust pastry is made by the rubbing-in method?
options: To coat the flour and give a short, crumbly texture
questions.explain: Fat coats the flour particles, shortening gluten strands to give a crumbly, 'short' texture.

questions.q: Whisking is a technique mainly used to:
options: Incorporate air into a mixture, such as cream or egg whites
questions.explain: Whisking incorporates air into mixtures such as cream and egg whites, creating volume and foam.

questions.q: To reduce the loss of water-soluble vitamins when cooking vegetables, you should:
options: Boil them for a very long time
Cook them in a small amount of water for a short time, or steam them
questions.explain: Using little water and short cooking times, or steaming, reduces vitamin loss into the cooking water.

questions.q: Steaming cooks food using:
questions.explain: Steaming cooks food using the steam (vapour) rising from boiling water, helping retain nutrients.

questions.q: Why is gentle simmering often preferred to fast boiling for cooking stews?
options: It cooks gently to avoid breaking up food and toughening meat
questions.explain: Gentle simmering cooks food evenly without breaking it up or toughening the protein as vigorous boiling can.

questions.q: Which traditional preservation method removes moisture so that bacteria cannot grow?
questions.explain: Drying (dehydration) removes water, preventing the bacteria growth that needs moisture.

questions.q: 'Rubbing-in' is a technique most commonly used when making:
questions.explain: Rubbing-in works fat into flour with the fingertips, used for pastry, crumbles and scones.

questions.q: Boiling cooks food by placing it in:
questions.explain: Boiling cooks food in water at 100C, the boiling point of water.

questions.q: Which method cooks food by submerging it in hot fat or oil?
questions.explain: Frying cooks food in hot fat or oil, which can increase the fat content of the food.

questions.q: The 'bridge hold' knife technique is used to:
options: Hold round foods steady so they can be cut safely
questions.explain: In the bridge hold, fingers form a bridge over the food so the knife can cut safely beneath.
